title: Automated Blendshape Personalization for Faithful Face Animations Using Commodity Smartphones
authors: Timo Menzel, Mario Botsch, Marc Erich Latoschik
venue: ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology
description:
Facial blendshapes are widely used in real-time applications for facial animation. They offer a straightforward way to animate faces of virtual characters by linearly combining a set of predefined example expressions. However, most characters models come with a generic set of blendshapes, that do not accurately represent the character's unique facial features, resulting in less convincing animations.
In this project, we present an automated pipeline to personalized facial blendshapes of a realistic character using smartphone input. We leverage Apple's ARKit framework to capture 52 example facial expressions corresponding to the ARKit blendshape set. With a position-based example-based facial rigging approach we then automatically generate personalized blendshapes that better represent the character's unique facial features, compared to the generic blendshapes and the popular original example-based facial rigging approach.
short_description: Improving facial expressions through automated blendshape personalization with smartphone input.

title: Avatars for the Masses: Smartphone-Based Reconstruction of Humans for Virtual Reality
authors: Timo Menzel, Erik Wolf, Stephan Wenninger, Niklas Spinczyk, Lena Holderrieth, Carolin Wienrich, Ulrich Schwanecke, Marc Erich Latoschik, Mario Botsch
description: During my PhD, I developed Avatars for the Masses (A4M) — a full-body avatar reconstruction system that uses smartphones to capture realistic, VR-ready avatars. The system consists of a mobile application that visually guides users through the scanning process and a complementary compute server that automatically reconstructs personalized avatars. The design ensures that even inexperienced users can capture scans of sufficient quality in uncontrolled, in-the-wild scenarios. Using a combination of segmentation, landmark detection, photogrammetry, and template fitting, the server generates a high-quality avatar in approximately 20 minutes. The system has been extensively evaluated, demonstrating results on par with expert-operated setups.
short_description: End-to-end smartphone-based system for full-body avatar reconstruction for VR.

title: Compensating Motion-Induced Errors in Smartphone-Based VR Avatar Reconstruction
authors: Friedemann Runte, Timo Menzel, Ulrich Schwanecke, Mario Botsch
venue: ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology
description: We refine our initial avatar reconstruction system (Avatars for the Masses) by addressing motion-induced errors during the scanning process. We observed that even a short two minute smartphone scan, results in significant motion artifacts. As we scan in A-pose, the photogrammetry assumption (i.e., an object is static during image capture) is often violated, as the arms tend to move. Through splitting the image sequence into multiple sub-sequences, called sub-scans, we can reduce these motion artifacts on a photogrammetric level. With these sub-scans, additional silhouette constraints, and a novel texture generation, we improve the reconstruction accuracy noticeably, even in more challenging scanning scenarios.
short_description: Motion during scanning causes photogrammetry software to produce artifacts. This project reduces these errors while keeping the scanning process user-friendly.
